title: Representable contractibility and homology of polynomial presentations
statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of $\mathcal U$-small commutative rings. Let $\mathcal D_{B/A}$ have objects all $\mathcal U$-small polynomial $A$-algebras $T$ with an $A$-algebra map $\epsilon_T:T\to B$, and arrows the $A$-algebra maps commuting with these maps to $B$; no surjectivity is required of $\epsilon_T$. This is a $\mathcal V$-small category. Let $Q_\bullet\to\operatorname{const}B$ be an augmented simplicial $\mathcal U$-small $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], with each $Q_n$ polynomial, whose underlying simplicial-set augmentation is a trivial Kan fibration [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. For any $T=A[E]\to B$ in $\mathcal D_{B/A}$ there is an isomorphism of simplicial sets
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D_{B/A}}(T,Q_\bullet)\cong\prod_{e\in E}\bigl(UQ_\bullet\times_{\operatorname{const}(UB)}\{\epsilon_T(e)\}\bigr),$$
where the right hand side consists of the generator images with their prescribed augmentations. Its map to a singleton is a trivial Kan fibration, and it is homotopy equivalent to that singleton. This holds also for empty and infinite $E$. For every $\mathcal V$-small commutative ring $R$ and covariant functor $F:\mathcal D_{B/A}\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$, form the derived colimit $\mathbf H(\mathcal D_{B/A},F)=\mathbf L\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal D_{B/A}}F$ in $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], using projective resolutions in the abelian functor category. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$a_Q^F:s(F(Q_\bullet))\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf H(\mathcal D_{B/A},F),$$
where $s(F(Q))^{-n}=F(Q_n)$, with alternating-face differential and zero positive terms. It is natural in $F$ and in augmented simplicial algebra maps $h:Q\to Q'$ between objects satisfying these hypotheses: $a_{Q'}^F\,s(F(h))=a_Q^F$. The comparison is the canonical one with the bar model of the derived colimit, whose degree $-n$ is $\bigoplus_{T_0\to\cdots\to T_n}F(T_0)$ and whose faces delete vertices, applying $F$ to the first arrow for the first face.

proof.text: Work in $\mathcal V$. The set of $\mathcal U$-small ring structures, algebra structures and augmentations is $\mathcal V$-small: each underlying set is an element of $\mathcal U$, and each structure is a finite tuple of functions between sets in $\mathcal U$. The polynomial objects form a subset, and the arrows form subsets of the corresponding function sets. Thus $\mathcal D_{B/A}$ is small in the working universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Augmentation compatibility says every operator $Q_n\to Q_m$ commutes with the maps to $B$, so $Q$ is a simplicial object of this category [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object].

source.place: Tag 08PS (lemma-identify-pi-shriek), polynomial presentation category, in the containing universe

proof.text: For $T=A[E]\to B$, send $f:T\to Q_n$ to $(f(e))_{e\in E}$. Its inverse evaluates a polynomial at the chosen generator images; every polynomial has finite support, so this works for arbitrary $E$. The condition $\epsilon_Qf=\epsilon_T$ holds exactly when $\epsilon_Q(f(e))=\epsilon_T(e)$ for all $e$, since both maps are $A$-algebra maps. Postcomposing $f$ with any simplicial operator acts componentwise on these images. Hence these inverse bijections give the stated simplicial isomorphism. When $E=\varnothing$ there is exactly one $A$-algebra map and the product is a singleton.

source.place: Tag 08PS (lemma-identify-pi-shriek), first half of proof: generator images and the product of fibres

proof.text: Write $X_b=UQ_\bullet\times_{\operatorname{const}(UB)}\{b\}$. A boundary map into $X_b$ gives a boundary in $UQ$ lying over the constant simplex $b$. The lifting property of $UQ\to\operatorname{const}(UB)$ supplies a simplex over $b$, hence a filler in $X_b$. Its degree-zero surjectivity supplies a vertex over $b$. Thus $X_b\to *$ satisfies [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. For a boundary in $\prod_eX_{\epsilon_T(e)}$, choose one such filler in each coordinate; their tuple is a simplicial filler, since all operators are componentwise. Likewise choose a vertex in every coordinate. Choice applies to the set $E$, including infinite $E$; the empty product has its unique filler and vertex. This proves that the displayed Hom simplicial set maps to $*$ by a trivial Kan fibration.

source.place: Tags 08NN (lemma-trivial-kan-base-change), 08NR (lemma-product-trivial-kan), with their boundary-lifting arguments written out

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence] to the map of step 3. Its statement supplies a section and a homotopy from the identity to section followed by projection. The other composite is the identity of $*$. Consequently $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D_{B/A}}(T,Q_\bullet)$ is homotopy equivalent to a singleton for every $T$.

Apply [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-colimit-computation] with working universe $\mathcal V$, $\mathcal D=\mathcal D_{B/A}$, the given $R,F$, and the simplicial object of step 1. Smallness is step 1 and its representable contractibility hypothesis is step 4. Its projective-resolution definition of $\mathbf H$ is exactly the one here. The resulting canonical isomorphism is $a_Q^F$; its source has precisely the stated alternating-face differential and vanishing positive terms, and its target has the stated first-vertex bar model. The same cited statement gives naturality in $F$.

For an augmented simplicial algebra map $h:Q\to Q'$, its components and augmentation compatibility give a simplicial morphism inside $\mathcal D_{B/A}$. Repeat steps 2--4 for $Q'$. In the compatibility formula of [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-colimit-computation] take $u=\mathrm{id}$, $\rho=\mathrm{id}_R$, $F'=F$, $\theta=\mathrm{id}_F$, and $k=h$. The displayed bar generator formula then sends every string and coefficient to itself, so $\mathbf H(u,\theta)=\mathrm{id}$. Its equality is exactly $a_{Q'}^F\,s(F(h))=a_Q^F$, with no choice of homotopy inverse entering the definition of either comparison.
